Junior year is your last chance to start meaningful activities that colleges notice. While everyone else has identical resumes, these will make you stand out completely. Activity number one, start a microbusiness that solves a real problem. I started a tutoring service for middle schoolers struggling with coding. I helped 10 students improve their skills and showed entrepreneurial initiative. Colleges eat this up because it demonstrates real -world and showed entrepreneurial initiative. Colleges eat this up because impact and leadership. Activity number two, create a community advocacy project. Find an issue in your local area and do something about it. You can organize specific campaigns and even present it to your city council. This shows initiative beyond just volunteering. Activity number three, become a certified expert in something unique. Get certified in CPR, become a lifeguard, learn coding languages or get photography credentials. These aren't just resume fillers. These are skills that demonstrate your commitment and can develop your real -world skills.
